commitResults.messageBody:
Added some new assertions, particularly to guard against null ptr
errors.

Parser.handleInput handles validation, parsing, command dispatch,
task creation, and persistence in one long method.

The mixed responsibilities make the command-processing flow harder to
read and maintain, and obscure the behavior of individual commands.

Split command processing into focused private methods for dispatch,
task-number operations, and task creation.

Keep the existing command behavior, response messages, and persistence
operations unchanged while reducing each method's level of
responsibility.

All tests and checkstyleMain pass under Java 25.

Main.start configures the entire JavaFX window in one long method.

The mixed setup responsibilities make the application startup flow harder
to read and maintain.

Split component creation, stage configuration, layout configuration, event
handler registration, and welcome-message display into focused methods.

Keep the existing initialization order and GUI behavior while making the
startup sequence easier to understand.

All tests and checkstyleMain pass under Java 25.

Task.initialise restores every task type and completion status in one
method while relying on raw storage literals.

The combined deserialization paths make the restoration logic harder to
read and allow task symbols and statuses to be interpreted
inconsistently.

Split restoration into task-type-specific helper methods and resolve
task symbols through TaskType.

Name the completion-status values to make the storage format explicit
while preserving the existing serialized representation and behavior.

All tests and checkstyleMain pass under Java 25.

TaskList repeats task-number validation and its error message in three
operations.

Duplicated validation can drift and makes changes to task-number
handling needlessly repetitive.

Reuse a shared task-index lookup and invalid-number response across
removal, marking, and unmarking.

Keep one-based command numbering and list-index behavior unchanged,
including removing the selected task by its original index.

All tests and checkstyleMain pass under Java 25.

Deadline and Event initialization use nested branches for validation,
parsing, and object setup.

The nested happy path makes task creation harder to follow, while null
checks on split results add noise without protecting the code.

Use guard clauses and simplify the validation expressions in both task
initializers.

Keep the existing input formats, error messages, date parsing, and
initialization behavior unchanged.

All tests and checkstyleMain pass under Java 25.

commitResults.messageTitle: Refactor list tasks to use streams
commitResults.messageBody:
Previously, used a for loop. It was relatively bulky, and a little hard
to understand.

Swap to stream paradigm, each step uses a known stream method, makes the
code more compact and easier to follow the chain of logic.
Add assertions
Improve code quality

Previously, a redundant check for valid task number was still present,
which should not be the case due to the assertion check. Also, assertion
check for null task list was moved to the helper index method instead
to make the code more reusable and general.
Refactor list tasks to use streams

commitResults.messageTitle: Update help command message and add test for it

commitResults.messageBody:
Task changes remain available in memory when a save fails, but the
command response reports success. A direct write can also damage the
existing save file if it is interrupted.

Return the save outcome and warn the user when persistence fails. Write
changes through a temporary file and replace the live file only after
the new content is complete. Use a regular replacement when atomic moves
are unavailable and remove temporary files after failed attempts.

Handle both I/O and access failures so storage problems do not crash the
application. Provide path-based overloads so storage failures can be
tested without using the real data file.

Storage records with unknown statuses, incorrect field counts, or broken
delimiters can be silently reinterpreted or skipped without useful
context. Partially initialized tasks can also enter the task list.

Validate each record as a complete sequence of fields. Require the exact
field count for its task type, a documented completion status, a
non-blank name, and valid subtype data.

Skip only the invalid record and report its line number. This preserves
valid tasks while making data corruption visible to the user.

An event accepts a start date that is equal to or later than its end
date. Such a period cannot represent the documented event duration.

Require the start date to be strictly earlier than the end date. Give a
specific error response so the user can correct the relationship between
the dates instead of troubleshooting their date format.

Command parsing depends on exact single spaces and ignores some extra
arguments. This causes equivalent whitespace to behave differently and
allows typing mistakes to produce unintended commands or task data.

Accept general whitespace between command elements while requiring each
command's documented parameters. Reject extra arguments for commands
that take none and require task numbers to contain only digits.

Require deadline and event fields in their documented structure. Trim
accepted values so incidental outer whitespace is not stored.

Whitespace-only todo names and search terms pass the empty-string
checks. This permits invisible tasks and misleading searches.

Treat blank values as missing input. Trim valid todo names and search
terms so display, matching, and persistence use the intended text.

Reading from a closed console input stream throws an exception, and an
unexpected command-processing failure can terminate the application
without a useful response.

Treat end-of-input as a normal exit through the existing cleanup path.
Catch unexpected runtime failures at the command boundary, retain their
diagnostic details, and return a safe message to the user.

The event pattern can absorb an earlier /from parameter into the task
name. A command containing repeated parameters can therefore create a
task with unintended details.

Require exactly one standalone /from parameter and one standalone /to
parameter before extracting event fields. This makes duplicate parameter
input fail consistently.

The test suite covers normal task creation and a small number of invalid
dates, but it does not protect the new parsing, storage, and application
boundary safeguards from regression.

Add tests for invalid date ranges, malformed parameters, blank values,
bad task numbers, console termination, and unexpected runtime failures.
Exercise corrupt records and failing paths with temporary storage so the
tests do not modify the user's real data file.

Provide package-private task-list and scanner injection points to keep
the boundary tests isolated without expanding the public API.

Task initializers detect the reason for invalid input, but print it only
to the console. The parser then replaces that detail with a generic
format message, leaving GUI users unable to tell what to correct.

Retain each task's validation error and return it through the normal
command response. Distinguish missing, repeated, and reordered
parameters; invalid start and end dates; invalid date ranges; and blank
task names.

Clarify task-number and find errors so each response describes the bad
value and gives the user a concrete next step. Avoid printing validation
messages inside task classes because the parser owns user interaction.

Add command-level tests for the exact error cases to ensure the useful
messages reach the user instead of being discarded.

commitResults.messageTitle: Storage: Surface load warnings in the GUI
commitResults.messageBody:
Storage load failures and malformed records are reported only in the
console. A GUI user sees an empty or incomplete task list without an
explanation, which can look like silent data loss.

Return an optional user-facing warning together with the loaded tasks.
Show that warning when the console or GUI starts. Retain detailed
diagnostics in the console for troubleshooting.

Summarize skipped records rather than exposing their stored contents.
Keep valid tasks available when only some records are malformed, and add
temporary-path tests for corrupt and inaccessible storage.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add coverage reporting and test infrastructure
commitResults.messageBody:
The test suite has no coverage report or parameterized test support.
Add JaCoCo and JUnit parameters to expose gaps and report each input
case separately. Exclude JavaFX classes reserved for manual checks.

commitResults.messageTitle: Isolate chatbot persistence for session tests
commitResults.messageBody:
Command tests save through a fixed path, which risks modifying real
user data and prevents reliable failure testing.

Allow each chatbot session to load and save through a supplied path.
Add integration tests for session isolation, task persistence, startup
warnings, and in-memory recovery after a failed save.

commitResults.messageTitle: Expand task validation and serialization tests
commitResults.messageBody:
Existing task tests leave calendar boundaries, completion transitions,
and several malformed inputs unchecked.

Cover null inputs, standalone parameters, leap days, stored records,
and every task symbol. Verify display and storage across completion
states so parsing and formatting regressions are visible.

commitResults.messageTitle: Cover task-list mutations and search behavior
commitResults.messageBody:
Task-list tests focus on invalid input and miss successful mutations.

Verify ordered listings, deletion and renumbering, repeated completion
changes, and boundary indices. Check search subsets and confirm that
invalid operations and searches preserve the original task list.

commitResults.messageTitle: Cover command dispatch and persistence failures
commitResults.messageBody:
Command validation tests do not verify successful dispatch or saved
state, and parser fixtures retain the default user-data destination.

Isolate all parser fixtures and cover every command, empty input,
reserved characters, numeric boundaries, and scanner cleanup. Assert
both state and responses, including recovery when persistence fails.

commitResults.messageTitle: Expand storage round-trip and recovery tests
commitResults.messageBody:
Storage tests cover a single todo round trip and only a few malformed
records, leaving replacement and recovery behavior under-specified.

Cover mixed task types, Unicode, completion states, empty replacement,
line endings, malformed records, unreadable encoding, and invalid
parent paths. Verify warnings and preservation of existing content.

Only the help text has direct UI assertions.

Capture console output to verify dividers, message overloads, and the
welcome banner. Restore the original stream after every capture so
these assertions do not interfere with other tests.

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix console exit behavior with lifecycle tests
commitResults.messageBody:
The console prints goodbye twice for bye and exits for uppercase BYE
even though the parser rejects it as an unknown command.

Make exit checks follow the parser's lowercase command rule and print
one goodbye. Apply the same exit rule to the GUI.

Test startup, EOF, invalid commands, persistence, and termination in
isolated child processes. Merge their coverage with JUnit coverage.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document automated coverage and manual GUI checks
commitResults.messageBody:
Coverage percentages need context to distinguish untested behavior
from unreachable code and platform-specific failure paths.

Document how to run the suite, inspect reports, and keep test data
isolated. Record the remaining coverage gaps and a pending manual GUI
checklist so reviewers can verify the excluded interaction behavior.
